name: OpenML Linear vs Non-linear Classifier Benchmark
description: A basic step for each data-mining or machine learning task is to determine which model to choose based on the problem and the data at hand. In this paper we investigate when non-linear classifiers outperform linear classifiers by means of a large scale experiment. We benchmark linear and non-linear versions of three types of classifiers (support vector machines; neural networks; and decision trees), and analyze the results to determine on what type of datasets the non-linear version performs better. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first principled and large scale attempt to support the common assumption that non-linear classifiers excel only when large amounts of data are available.
reputation: A well-known experimental study using OpenML datasets; cited in model-selection and data-centric ML discussions though not a fixed leaderboard dataset.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark spanning many OpenML datasets of varying size and difficulty; results are highly dataset-dependent. Not a single standardized leaderboard — outcomes depend on dataset characteristics (size, noise, feature types).
